chunks: Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, created the believer from the clay of Paradise, and created the disbeliever from the clay of the Fire.

And he (AS) said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, intends goodness for a servant, He purifies his soul and his body, so he does not hear anything of good except that he recognizes it, and he does not hear anything of evil except that he rejects it.

He (the narrator) said: And I heard him (AS) saying: The clays are three (types) — the clay of the Prophets, and the believer is from that clay, except that the Prophets are from its purest part; they are the root and for them is their excellence, and the believers are the branches from a sticky clay. Likewise, God, Mighty and Majestic, will not separate between them and their Shia.

And he (AS) said: The clay of the Nasibi is from black fashioned mud; and as for the weak ones (in understanding), they are from dust. No believer turns away from his faith, nor does a Nasibi turn away from his enmity, and God's Will prevails regarding them.

key_terms.المستضعفون: the spiritually/religiously weak or undiscerning — those who lack the clarity to commit fully to either faith or enmity
key_terms.المشيئة: the divine Will or Volition — God's ultimate authority over the final spiritual state of all created beings
key_terms.الناصب: Nasibi — one who harbors active enmity toward the Ahlulbayt (household of the Prophet); a technical term in Shia theology
key_terms.صفوتها: the elite/purest portion — the Prophets are described as being from the most refined part of the believing clay
key_terms.طينة: primordial clay — the cosmic substance from which different categories of human beings were created, determining their fundamental spiritual orientation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the clay from which believers and disbelievers were created?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches a cosmological doctrine of human origins based on primordial clay: believers were fashioned from the clay of Paradise, disbelievers from the clay of the Fire, and Prophets from the purest portion of the believers' clay. This teaching, addressed to early Shia communities seeking to understand why some people are inclined toward good and others toward evil, presents a predestinarian framework while affirming divine will as the ultimate authority over all outcomes. The doctrine of three types of clay — prophetic, believing, and hostile — was a key element of early Shia theology regarding the nature of faith and enmity.
